scope: Add SSO enforcement to Kestrel workspace security settings

facts.statement: Kestrel is a B2B customer support platform with Starter, Growth and Scale plans.
SSO is included only on the Scale plan; Starter and Growth do not include it.
The current security route and settings navigation are restricted to the Owner role.
The help center, last reviewed in August 2025, says workspace Admins can connect an identity provider and require SSO.
The current implementation and the help center disagree about whether Admins can manage SSO.
The current security panel is a disabled 'Coming soon' placeholder with no connection form.
The inspected SSO connection model has no enforcement flag, enforcement timestamp or session-revocation hook.
The customer request is to require SSO for every member, not merely to offer SSO as an option.
The brief assigns billing, workspace deletion and security enforcement to Owners, and member and workspace configuration to Admins.
Support themes show Admins expect to manage SSO and customers fear locking everyone out.
Plan changes are handled by the account team; there is no in-app purchase flow.
The help center tells customers to contact Kestrel support if the identity provider is unavailable.

assumptions.statement: A workspace has one identity-provider connection.
assumptions.source: Inferred from the single-connection model in evidence/app/src/auth/sso.ts

assumptions.statement: Owners should retain the final enforcement decision because lockout risk is a workspace-level security action.
assumptions.source: Inferred from the role boundaries in evidence/product-brief.md and the lockout theme in evidence/support-themes.md

assumptions.statement: 'Require SSO' is clearer than 'Enable SSO' for the irreversible-feeling action.
assumptions.source: Inferred from the support theme about session uncertainty

unknowns.statement: Whether enforcement applies to existing sessions immediately or at the next sign-in.
unknowns.source: No session behavior exists in the inspected code; the help center only mentions the next sign-in.

unknowns.statement: What recovery path exists if the identity provider is unavailable or misconfigured.
unknowns.source: No break-glass flow exists in the inspected code or documentation.

unknowns.statement: Whether enforcement may remain on after a workspace leaves the Scale plan.
unknowns.source: Plan entitlements and enforcement are not connected in the inspected code.

unknowns.statement: Whether members can belong to more than one identity-provider domain.
unknowns.source: Only a single-provider connection is evidenced.

questions.question: Who may turn SSO enforcement on and off: only Owners, or Owners and Admins?
questions.why_it_matters: This changes the route guard, the controls Admins see, the audit trail and the lockout recovery path.
options: Admins configure the connection; Owners enforce

questions.question: What recovery path should exist if the identity provider is unavailable or misconfigured?
questions.why_it_matters: Without a recovery path, an enforcement mistake can lock every member out of the workspace.
options: No bypass; wait for the identity provider to recover

questions.question: Should enforcement apply to existing sessions immediately or at the next sign-in?
questions.why_it_matters: Immediate revocation is stricter but can interrupt active support shifts.

questions.question: Should the security page show the SAML metadata URL and entity ID?
questions.why_it_matters: This helps Admins verify configuration but may expose implementation detail.

questions.question: How should a downgrade from Scale behave while enforcement is on?
questions.why_it_matters: A silent downgrade could disable enforcement or leave members unable to sign in.

blocking_gaps: Q2: no safe recovery path is defined
